replacements.old_heading: The Mushroom Kingdom Learns to Travel
replacements.old_body: On October 23, 1988, Super Mario Bros. 3 was released in Japan for Famicom. The North American and European versions would arrive in 1990 and 1991 respectively, so this date concerns the Japanese debut only. Nintendo radically expands the grammar of the first Super Mario games by introducing world maps, alternate routes, an item inventory, and transformations such as Raccoon Mario, Frog Mario, and Tanooki Mario. The ability to fly grows from a documented design compromise: flight had to be free enough to feel like a new conquest, but limited enough not to make levels built on the ground irrelevant. The game thus alternates surprise and control, turning each world into a small repertoire of rules, themes, and variations that would influence Nintendo platformers for years.

replacements.old_heading: A Fleet Carries Its Home With It
replacements.old_body: On September 28, 1999, Homeworld was released in the United States for Windows, published by Sierra and developed by Relic Entertainment. The series' official chronology identifies this date as the debut of the first entry; European distribution followed later, so it should not be treated as a worldwide release. Homeworld brings real-time strategy into truly three-dimensional space, forcing players to think above and below the usual plane of the map. But its identity also grows from the continuity of the fleet: ships, losses and resources carry across missions and turn the campaign into a material journey. The mothership, the story of exile and a soundtrack designed to suggest distance and solemnity make space warfare a story of collective survival rather than military expansion alone.

replacements.old_heading: The City Measures Who You Can Trust
replacements.old_body: On October 22, 1999, Grand Theft Auto 2 was released in the United Kingdom on PlayStation and Windows. The North American dates came later, so October 22 should be treated as a British regional release, not a worldwide launch. Developed by DMA Design and published under the Rockstar Games label, the game retains the top-down view of the first Grand Theft Auto but organizes Anywhere City around seven rival gangs. The respect system links missions to territorial consequences: helping one group can make its rivals more hostile. The city thus becomes a network of reputations as well as streets. GTA2 preserves a structure that is less remembered today than the three-dimensional installments, but it already shows the series' interest in urban worlds crossed by factions, radio, traffic, and systemic reactions.

replacements.old_body: On September 24, 2001, Ico was released in North America for PlayStation 2, published by Sony Computer Entertainment America. Japan would receive it in December and Europe in 2002, so this date should not be presented as a worldwide release. Fumito Ueda's first game as director deliberately reduces many familiar signs of the adventure genre: few explanations, a discreet interface, long architectural spaces and a relationship built mainly through movement. Holding Yorda's hand is not a scene to watch, but a command used to cross the castle together. Architecture therefore becomes a measure of the distance between two bodies, while light, silence and depth of field give the place an unusual solidity. Ico shows how subtraction can become a precise form of design.

replacements.old_body: On September 18, 2008, the PlayStation 3 version of Eternal Sonata was released in Japan, published by Bandai Namco under the title Trusty Bell: Chopin no Yume Reprise. It was not the game's first release, since the Xbox 360 version had arrived in 2007: this anniversary refers specifically to the expanded Japanese PS3 edition. tri-Crescendo's project builds a role-playing game around the imagined final moments of Fryderyk Chopin's life, but avoids reducing music to mere biographical decoration. Light and shadow alter combat, musical names run through characters and places, and the score works together with color and rhythm. The result is a work in which the language of the concert becomes material for organizing space, systems and tone.

replacements.old_heading: The Sea Holds the Choices Together
replacements.old_body: On October 5, 2018, Assassin's Creed Odyssey was released globally on PlayStation 4, Xbox One and PC. Ubisoft distinguishes this date from the October 2 early access reserved for certain editions, so October 5 represents the standard commercial launch. Developed mainly by Ubisoft Québec, Odyssey takes the series to fifth-century BCE Greece and expands the importance of dialogue choices, role-playing progression and naval travel. The player can choose Kassandra or Alexios, build relationships and take on assignments in a world that mixes historical reconstruction and myth. The scale of the archipelago does not simply multiply activities: sea, mountains and cities organize different tempos of travel. The adventure becomes a long negotiation between personal identity, war and the telling of the past.
